data.name: Nitish
data.gender_notes: Nitish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words 'nit' (intellect, mind) and 'ish' (lord), Nitish means 'Lord of the mind' or 'Lord of intellect'. This name is associated with wisdom, knowledge, and enlightenment. The name Nitish carries the meaning “Lord of the mind, intellect” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nitish usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the mind, intellect and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes inner wisdom and mental strength.
data.etymology: Nitish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the mind, intellect.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nitish total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

The name encourages individuals to tap into their inner intellect and use it to seek truth, understanding, and inner peace. historical_references.reference: Nitish Kumar was born on 1 March 1961 in Bakhtiarpur, Bihar, India. He was educated at Patna High School and later studied at St. Xavier's College in Calcutta and the Indian Institute of Technology in Kharagpur. He began his political career as a member of the Janata Dal party, but later formed his own party, the Janata Dal (United). He has been the Chief Minister of Bihar since 2005.

The name Nitish is of Sanskrit origin and means 'leader' or 'guide'. It is a common name among Hindus and has been borne by various historical figures. One such figure is Nitish Sena, who was a prominent Jain monk and scholar during the Gupta Empire (c. 320-550 CE). He is known for his contributions to Jain literature, particularly his commentary on the Tattvartha Sutra.
